audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] tells the player 'the blade cast is not a clean projectile Windwall can fully eat'. Both kit files say the opposite: Flawless Duet is flagged projectile, and Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds'.
audit.why: Irelia kit, E: 'projectile — can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects'. Yasuo kit, W: 'blocksProjectiles — deletes enemy projectile damage entirely', 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', cooldown 25/23/21/19/17. Vanguard's Edge carries the same projectile flag. Telling the player their stun goes through the wall is the single most punishing possible error in this matchup.
audit.corrected: The blades are projectiles and Wind Wall eats them — bait the 25s W before spending E or R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was given to Irelia in both layers while whys[0] calls it a coinflip, and 2+ items was given to Irelia while whys[6], spikes[3] and the whole late section say Yasuo out-scales her.
audit.why: Two crit items plus Wind Wall blanking her blades and a Steel Tempest knockup into Last Breath is a clear Yasuo late game. 51.19% over 1432 games is an early-to-mid Irelia lane that decays.
audit.corrected: Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Irelia, Skill, Yasuo — matched pairs both layers.

audit.why: Irelia at 2, 3 and 6; Yasuo at two crit items. Level 6 phrasing was already keyed to Wind Wall and Q3 being spent, which is the right sequencing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Do's card named Last Breath as the tracked cooldown but gave no number, and the tracked cooldown that actually governs Irelia's engage is Wind Wall, not R.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30s and only fires off an existing knockup; Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s and is what deletes her engage. Steel Tempest is a 4s cooldown that knocks up at 2 stacks. Sweeping Blade recasts on 0.5s down to 0.1s but cannot re-target the same enemy immediately.
audit.corrected: Do's now gives Last Breath's 70s-to-30s range and its knockup prerequisite; Don'ts now explain the two-stack Steel Tempest tell and Sweeping Blade's recast speed.

edits.before: Stack passive on the wave before any trade. Identify how Yasuo contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coinflip — stack passive on the wave, and never throw a cast into a Yasuo holding Wind Wall.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Yasuo carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two crit items and he takes over: Wind Wall blanks your blades and a Q3 knockup into Last Breath ends your dash chain.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Yasuo carry threat 9/10.
edits.after: Hard matchup — difficulty 6/10, Yasuo carry threat 9/10.

edits.before: His all-in after a knockup. While down, you win. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Last Breath only follows a knockup — 70s at rank 1, and just 30s at rank 3. Bait it.

edits.before: That is Yasuo's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks make the next cast a knockup — count his Q hits.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade recasts in 0.1s — he kites your whole reset chain.

edits.before: E (Flawless Duet) online — your first hard-CC window. Place the second blade BEHIND him so the stun lands even if he tries to E-dash out, then Q-reset in; the blade cast is not a clean projectile Windwall can fully eat.
edits.after: E (Flawless Duet) online — your first hard-CC window. Place the second blade BEHIND him so the stun lands even if he E-dashes out, then Q-reset in. The blades are projectiles: Wind Wall eats them, so bait the 25s W first.

notes: Most dangerous correction in this slice: spikes[1] claimed Wind Wall could not fully eat Irelia's E blades. Both kit files disagree — Flawless Duet is a projectile, Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles for 4s. Vanguard's Edge carries the same projectile flag, so the R engage is equally deniable; the rest of the page already advises baiting W first, which is now consistent. report[14] said 'Even matchup' while diff is HARD — relabelled.
